\viewkind4\uc1\pard\cf1\ul\fs24 ACTION 1:\ulnone\par
By unanimous consent, the Council Rules were suspended to allow Lish Whitson, Council Central Staff, to address the Council.\par
\par
\ul ACTION 2:\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Council President Hollingsworth and duly seconded to amend Council Bill 121215, Section 1, as shown in Attachment 2 to the Minutes.\par
\par
The motion carried by the following vote:\par
In favor: 9 - Foster, Hollingsworth, Juarez, Kettle, Lin, Rinck, Rivera, Saka, Strauss\par
Opposed: None\par
\par
\ul ACTION 3:\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Saka and duly seconded to amend Council Bill 121215 as shown in Attachment 3 to the Minutes.\par
\par
The motion failed by the following vote:\par
In favor: 1 - Saka\par
Opposed: 8 - Foster, Hollingsworth, Juarez, Kettle, Lin, Rinck, Rivera, Strauss\par
\par
\ul ACTION 4:\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Lin and duly seconded to amend Council Bill 121215 as shown in Attachment 4 to the Minutes.\par
\par
The motion carried by the following vote:\par
In favor: 7 - Foster, Hollingsworth, Kettle, Lin, Rinck, Saka, Strauss\par
Opposed: 2 - Juarez, Rivera\par
\par
\ul ACTION 5:\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Lin and duly seconded to amend Council Bill 121215 as shown in Attachment 5 to the Minutes.\par
\par
The motion carried by the following vote:\par
In favor: 8 - Foster, Hollingsworth, Kettle, Lin, Rinck, Rivera, Saka, Strauss\par
Opposed: 1 - Juarez\par
\par
\ul ACTION 6:\ulnone\par
Motion was made by Councilmember Kettle and duly seconded to amend the recitals in Council Bill 121215 and add a new Section 9, as shown in the underlined and strike through language below:\par
\par
\ul The State of California has developed guidance for specific topics to guide analysis of impacts under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).\par
The City of New York has developed a technical manual to guide analysis of proposals under the City Environmental Quality Review.\par
Unlike some states, like California, or cities, like New York City, neither Washington State nor the City of Seattle have developed detailed guidance on how SEPA analysis should be performed, resulting in each environmental impact statement using different approaches to analyze possible impacts.\par
Clear and uniform SEPA guidelines can increase clarity, trust, and consistency in environmental documents.\ulnone\par
\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\cf0\kerning2\f1 The Land Use Code requires \strike\f2 the development of\strike0\f1  director\rquote s reports for Type IV and V Council land use decisions but does not \ul clearly\ulnone  contemplate \ul reports for\ulnone  Council-sponsored land use decisions.\par
\pard\sa160\sl276\slmult1\qc * * *\par
\pard\cf1\kerning0\ul\f0 Section 9. The Office of Planning and Community Development (OPCD) should consult with other City agencies and City Boards and Commissions to develop a report on options for the creation of uniform guidelines for review under the City of Seattle\rquote s SEPA Policies, Seattle Municipal Code Section 25.05.675. OPCD should provide its report by March 1, 2027 and provide a briefing to the Land Use and Sustainability Committee or the City Council. The report should include:\par
1. An inventory of existing resources available to support analysis of specific elements of the environment, consistent with the City\rquote s environmental policies, including guidance provided by State agencies.\par
2. A recommendation on whether to prepare guidance for analysis of specific elements of the environment, or for a more comprehensive set of guidelines covering all elements of the environment.\par
3. If the report recommends development of uniform guidance on a subset of the elements of the environment, a prioritized list of elements.\par
4. A timeline and costs for implementing the recommendations of the report.\ulnone\par
\par
The motion carried by the following vote:\par
In favor: 9 - Foster, Hollingsworth, Juarez, Kettle, Lin, Rinck, Rivera, Saka, Strauss\par
Opposed: None\par
\par
